memories.content: The user stores copies of identity documents in an encrypted folder.
On a day the user transferred between buses twice, they rested for an hour after the trip.
On a day the user took a direct route with a similar travel time, they remained seated to the destination.
After arriving at an entrance with stairs only, the user went around to an entrance on the other side of the building.
On a day the user checked the accessible entrance location in advance, they arrived before the agreed time.
On a rainy day, the user's clothes became wet while crossing an uncovered section at a transfer stop.
On a day the user traveled with their maternal uncle, they agreed to meet at an entrance near the elevator.
The user's maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat from which it is easy to stand during long-distance travel.
The local agent cannot know whether an accessible entrance is operating that day from past route records alone.
The transfer route the user takes has more boarding and alighting events and walking segments than the direct route.
The user keeps the shared laundry-room access card in an entrance drawer.
The user went downstairs 25 minutes after the laundry finished and received a note from another household.
For the next load, the user set a reminder five minutes before the end and removed the laundry immediately.
The user washed light-colored clothes with new jeans, and color transferred onto white socks.
The user later washed the new jeans separately, and the color of the other clothes did not change.
On a day the user did not check the dryer filter, the clothes needed another drying cycle.
On the next use, after emptying the filter, the user finished drying in one cycle.
The building manager judges that not leaving finished laundry for a long time is fair to other households.
When creating a shared laundry-room reminder, base it on the end time of the machine the user started.
Even if the local agent knows where the card is kept, it cannot know which machines in the shared laundry room are currently available.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate practical domains: the reference describes document security, accessible travel, route burden, and a relative’s preferences, while the compared frame describes shared-laundry access, timing, sorting, drying, fairness, and live machine uncertainty. No cross-frame operational claims align or conflict.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-only information about document security, with no compared-side claim addressing that decision.
relations.summary: The user stores identity-document copies in an encrypted folder.

relations.reason: The transfer-day recovery, seated direct journey, and structural route differences split one reference-only claim about relative travel burden; the compared frame contains no travel-routing counterpart.
relations.summary: The user’s experiences distinguish the greater physical burden of a transfer route from a similarly timed direct route.

relations.reason: The reactive detour and successful advance check split one reference-only claim about accessible-entrance planning; no compared-side memory addresses building-entry navigation.
relations.summary: Accessible-entrance location affects the user’s navigation and punctuality.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-only information about weather exposure during travel.
relations.summary: An uncovered transfer-stop section exposed the user to rain and wet clothing.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-only information about travel meeting coordination.
relations.summary: When traveling together, the user and their maternal uncle agreed to meet near an elevator entrance.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-only information about the uncle’s seating preference.
relations.summary: The user’s maternal uncle prefers an aisle seat that makes standing easier on long-distance trips.

relations.reason: This is a reference-only limitation concerning live entrance status; machine availability in the compared frame governs a different operational decision.
relations.summary: Past route records cannot establish whether an accessible entrance is operating on a particular day.

relations.reason: This is independently useful compared-only information about access-card storage, distinct from storage of identity documents.
relations.summary: The shared laundry-room access card is kept in an entrance drawer.

relations.reason: The delayed collection, successful reminder, fairness judgment, and reminder rule split one compared-only claim about timely removal from shared machines.
relations.summary: Laundry reminders should follow the user’s machine end time so finished loads are removed promptly and fairly.

relations.reason: The contrasting washes jointly support one compared-only claim about separating new jeans to protect lighter clothes.
relations.summary: Washing new jeans separately prevented the color transfer seen when they were mixed with light clothing.

relations.reason: The two uses split one compared-only claim about the filter’s relevance to drying performance.
relations.summary: Emptying the dryer filter was associated with finishing in one cycle rather than requiring another cycle.

relations.reason: This is a compared-only limitation concerning live machine availability; accessible-entrance operation in the reference frame governs a different decision.
relations.summary: Knowing the access-card location does not reveal which shared laundry machines are currently available.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only information concerns laundry-room access, prompt and fair collection, color-safe sorting, dryer-filter effects, and uncertainty about current machine availability.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only information concerns secure document storage, travel effort and weather exposure, accessible-entrance planning and uncertainty, and the maternal uncle’s meeting and seating preferences.
